explain.say: Look at the two letters on the board. They are b and d. They look alike, so many people mix them up. You will learn two ways to tell them apart.

explain.say: Here is the bed trick. Make two fists with your thumbs up. Push your knuckles together. Your left hand makes b. Your right hand makes d. Your hands look like a bed.
The word bed starts with b and ends with d. Your hands make the same shape. When you are unsure, make your hand bed and check. Today, write bed 3 times and say each sound.

faq.a: Make two fists with thumbs up and push your knuckles together. Your left hand makes b, your right hand makes d, and together they look like a bed.
asks: How does the bed trick work?

faq.a: Think bat and ball. The bat, the tall line, comes first. Then the ball, the bump, sits on the right.
Think drum and drumstick. The round drum comes first, then the tall stick. A d also starts with a c shape.

faq.q: Why do b and d get mixed up?
faq.a: They are the same shape, flipped. A flipped cup is still a cup. But a flipped b becomes a d. Practice helps a lot.
asks: Why do I mix up b and d?

faq.q: What else helps with b and d?
faq.a: Trace big letters in sand or with your finger on the table, and say the sound as you trace. A teacher or grown-up can stick a little bed picture on your desk to check.
asks: More tips for b and d

facts: The letters b and d are mirror images of each other.
In the word bed, b comes first and d comes last, so the tall lines stand at each end like bedposts.

quiz.say: Which one has a tall line first, then a bump?
quiz.show: Tall line first, then a bump. Which one?
quiz.why: You write b with the tall line first, then the bump. Think bat, then ball.

wrong.0: d starts with the bump, then the tall line.
wrong.2: p has its line going down below the writing line.

quiz.say: Make the bed with your fists. Which one makes d?
quiz.show: ✊✊ Bed trick: which fist makes d?
quiz.why: Your right hand makes d. The d comes at the end of bed.

wrong.0: Your left hand makes b, the first letter of bed.
wrong.1: Each hand makes one letter: b on the left, d on the right.
